source_text: Ἀλλὰ μόνον κρατείτω ἐν ὑμῖν ἡ ἐν Νικαίᾳ παρὰ τῶν Πατέρων ὁμολογηθεῖσα πίστις· ἐν ᾗ καὶ πάντες καὶ τῶν νῦν μαχομένων πρὸς αὐτὴν παρῆσαν Πατέρες, καθὰ προείπομεν, καὶ ὑπέγραψαν· ἵνα καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὁ Ἀπόστολος εἴπῃ· Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ὅτι πάντα μου μέμνησθε, καὶ καθὼς παρέδωκα ὑμῖν τὰς παραδόσεις, οὕτω κατέχετε. Αὕτη γὰρ ἡ ἐν Νικαίᾳ σύνοδος, ἀληθῶς στηλογραφία κατὰ πάσης αἱρέσεώς ἐστιν. Αὕτη καὶ τοὺς βλασφημοῦντας εἰς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ λέγοντας αὐτὸ κτίσμα, ἀνατρέπει. Εἰρηκότες γὰρ οἱ Πατέρες περὶ τῆς εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν πίστεως, ἐπήγαγον εὐθύς· Πιστεύομεν καὶ εἰς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἵνα, τελείαν καὶ πλήρη τὴν εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν Τριάδα πίστιν ὁμολογήσαντες, τὸν χαρακτῆρα τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ πίστεως, καὶ τὴν διδασκαλίαν τῆς Καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἐν τούτῳ γνωρίσωσι. Δῆλον γὰρ καὶ παρ' ὑμῖν καὶ παρὰ πᾶσι καθέστηκε· καὶ οὐδεὶς ἂν Χριστιανῶν ἀμφίβολον εἰς τοῦτο σχοίη τὴν διάνοιαν, ὡς οὐκ ἔστιν ἡμῶν ἡ πίστις εἰς τὴν κτίσιν, ἀλλ' εἰς ἕνα Θεὸν Πατέρα παντοκράτορα, πάντων ὁρατῶν τε καὶ ἀοράτων ποιητήν· καὶ εἰς ἕνα Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν, τὸν Υἱὸν αὐτοῦ τὸν μονογενῆ· καὶ εἰς ἓν Πνεῦμα ἅγιον· ἕνα Θεὸν τὸν ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ τελείᾳ Τριάδι γινωσκόμενον· εἰς ἣν καὶ βαπτιζόμενοι, καὶ ἐν ταύτῃ συναπτόμενοι τῇ θεότητι, πιστεύομεν καὶ κληρονομῆσαι βασιλείαν οὐρανῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, δι' οὗ τῷ Πατρὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Nicaea alone is the sufficient confession of the Triune faith
orientation: Athanasius is closing his letter to the African bishops, urging them to hold only the faith confessed at Nicaea, which he says overthrows every heresy, including those who call the Holy Spirit a creature.
pass_a_gloss: But only let the faith confessed at Nicaea by the Fathers prevail among you; in which also all the Fathers, even of those now fighting against it, were present, as we said before, and signed; so that also about us the Apostle may say: Now I praise you, because you remember me in all things, and just as I handed down to you the traditions, so you hold them fast. For this council at Nicaea is truly an inscription against every heresy. This also overthrows those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit and say that it is a creature. For the Fathers, having spoken about the faith in the Son, immediately added: We believe also in the Holy Spirit, so that, having confessed the complete and full faith in the Holy Trinity, they might make known in this the imprint of the faith in Christ and the teaching of the Catholic Church. For it has become clear both among you and among all; and no one of Christians would hold a doubtful mind about this, that our faith is not in the creation, but in one God the Father almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible; and in one Lord Jesus Christ, his only-begotten Son; and in one Holy Spirit; one God known in the holy and perfect Trinity; into which also being baptized, and in this being joined to the divinity, we believe also to inherit the kingdom of the heavens in Christ Jesus our Lord, through whom to the Father be the glory and the might unto the ages. Amen.

choices.why: The word means a public inscription on a stone pillar or stele; rendering it as 'inscription' preserves the image of a permanent public record that stands against every heresy.
The glossary requires 'imprint' for χαρακτήρ, used here of the faith's exact stamp or mark.
The glossary requires 'creature' for κτίσμα, used here of the Arian claim about the Holy Spirit.
Here κτίσις refers to the created order as a whole, not an individual creature; 'creation' captures the contrast with the uncreated Trinity.
The plural 'traditions' matches the Pauline quotation and preserves the sense of handed-down teachings.
The participle is passive/middle and the dative expresses union with the divine nature; 'being joined to the divinity' keeps the theological force of participation through baptism.

pass_b_english: But let only the faith confessed at Nicaea by the Fathers hold sway among you. In that council, as we said before, all the Fathers were present—even those now fighting against it—and they signed. So the Apostle may say about us: “I praise you because you remember me in everything and hold firmly to the traditions just as I handed them on to you” (1 Corinthians 11:2). For this council at Nicaea is truly an inscription set up against every heresy. It also overthrows those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit and call the Spirit a creature. For after the Fathers spoke about faith in the Son, they immediately added: “We believe also in the Holy Spirit,” so that by confessing a complete and full faith in the Holy Trinity they might make known in this the imprint of faith in Christ and the teaching of the Catholic Church. For it is clear both among you and among all people, and no Christian would hold a doubtful mind about this: our faith is not in creation, but in one God, the Father Almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible; and in one Lord Jesus Christ, his only-begotten Son; and in one Holy Spirit—one God known in the holy and perfect Trinity. Baptized into this Trinity and being joined to the divinity in it, we believe that we will also inherit the kingdom of heaven in Christ Jesus our Lord, through whom to the Father be glory and might forever. Amen.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'you remember me in all things' or 'all my ways', not 'me in everything'.
